summary: A is substantially closer to the frozen contract and far more scope-disciplined, although it still duplicates Add instead of routing through it and lacks required validation/source-error tests.
reasons: A adds exactly the requested Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field "file", buffers into a replayable body, and leaves Add and retry machinery unchanged.
B explicitly violates the contract by adding association fields and WithFilesFormFields, changing FilesOption behavior, and refactoring global request/retry and reader-ownership semantics.
Both Upload implementations bypass FilesService.Add and duplicate its request/response logic, contrary to the required reuse path.
A’s retry test confirms multiple attempts but does not inspect the retried multipart payload; its ordinary upload test separately verifies field, filename, and content.
risks_a: Upload bypasses Add, so option handling and error behavior can drift between the two methods.
No tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.
The retry test only counts requests and does not prove the multipart content is intact on retry.
risks_b: Adds forbidden association-form functionality and a new public FilesOption.
Changes global Raw.Do retry behavior and body-closing ownership outside the task’s allowed scope.

enableBodyReplay reuses and seeks the same reader for every body, creating fragile semantics and potential concurrency hazards during retry handling or redirects/transport behavior that overlap body lifetimes or close calls indirectly; closing semantics are intentionally overridden globally for seekable readers only, making ownership behavior reader-type-dependent and surprising to callers and transports relying on standard request body lifecycle behavior. These changes are unrelated to the Upload contract and expand regression risk substantially. Also, the helper’s seek-to-end probe can mutate readers and may fail to restore position if SeekEnd fails after movement, while the implementation silently treats some seek failures as one-shot. Additionally, setting GetBody around one mutable reader does not create independent bodies as net/http generally expects, so concurrent or overlapping replay consumers can interfere. The change also adds Content-Length based on end-start, altering transfer behavior for all seekable bodies. Finally, raw.Do callers passing os.File previously had it closed by the request lifecycle; this patch silently changes resource ownership and can leak descriptors in existing code that relied on the old behavior.
